input.body:
label: bug
file: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

The `handleClick` handler only resets `busy` back to `false` in the success path of `exportReport(...).then(...)`. Since `exportReport` throws on a non-2xx response (and rejects on other errors like network failures), a failed export never clears `busy`, leaving the button (and format select) permanently disabled until the page is reloaded. The fix is to also reset `busy` in a `.catch(...)` (or `.finally(...)`) handler, and probably surface an error toast to the user in that case.

input.title: Reset export button state after a failed export
input.body: File: src/components/ExportButton.tsx. The handleClick function's call to exportReport only has a .then() handler, so when the returned promise rejects (e.g. the server responds with a non-2xx status and exportReport throws), setBusy(false) is never called and the button stays disabled until the page is reloaded. Add a .catch() (or try/catch) that resets busy to false and shows an error toast on failure, so the button becomes clickable again after a failed export.
